reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion but replaces getNextDate's applyWeekendRule call with inline policy and implements daily filtering separately in getDatesInRange.

duplication.why: Forward and reverse daily filtering repeat the same traversal structure, weekend movement reimplements existing policy, and the range handler independently decides daily exclusions.

placement.why: Handler registration and configuration types fit their existing layers, but business-day policy is split between shared scheduling code and the server handler instead of residing in the shared rule abstraction.

scope.why: All edits concern the requested schedule rules, range handler, configuration field, or associated tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate separate occurrence-adjustment implementations, duplicated traversal loops, and a range-padding assumption coupled to weekend-only movement.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate replaces applyWeekendRule with inline movement; packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts:getDatesInRange decides daily exclusions outside that abstraction.

disguised_duplication.where: getNextDate reshapes getDateWithSkippedWeekend/applyWeekendRule movement into directional iteration, while getDatesInRange expresses the daily exclusion decision separately through filtering and a computed skipWeekend flag.

abstraction_drift.where: getNextDate adds daily-specific branches for forward filtering, reverse fallback filtering, and final adjustment; it bypasses applyWeekendRule, while getDatesInRange independently implements daily policy and getUpcomingDates retains the existing helper.
